claims: search/packer/candidates/s299-1025.cert states s(299) <= 8901847717666168847717657266821/(5*10^29) = 17.803695435332337694...; issue #824 (opened 2026-10-26T03:52:18Z by evand) reports it rounded up at 12 places, 17.803695435333, 1.92e-2 below the register's 33/2 + sqrt(7)/2 = 17.822875655533 (the Kingbird catalogue), and prints its SHA-256.

The certificate's header calls it a dilation (dilate_cert.py, delta 1e-12) of the binary64 packing s299-1025.input.txt, side 17.803695435314534. Its JSON report states that the exact solver did not certify a KKT point: cert_valid false, a pair (235, 281) overlapping by 0.711 at the 80-digit point s299-1025.exact.txt, which is therefore no packing. The issue says local optimality is not established and that a corner-corner MILP linearization suggests a descent the source did not realise.

The issue calls it 'a new packing (not a refinement of the register's 33/2 + sqrt(7)/2 construction), built by a fault-line composition: our independent implementation of Chris Deotte's multi-gadget fault DP, described in his Kaggle notebooks', and asks that Chris Deotte be credited for the method and for the start, the s(334) packing (side 18.795715128) in his public Kaggle notebook 'squares-in-squares-ftmc-milp-refill-22-311'.

The issue says the source's two exact checkers, search/exact/verify_cert.py (separating axes) and verify_cert2.py (polygon intersection), both print VALID, and that they share an author and the certificate format.

The issue quotes two Kaggle per-puzzle leaderboard entries that state a side and no packing: 17.802718854399 for team Amin (2026-10-23 00:15 UTC, also in Francisco Couzo's upper_bounds.json as a reported bound) and 17.798169713703 for team Chris Deotte (2026-10-25 02:30 UTC), both below this certificate's side. Those statements are the author's; no source program ran here.
